messages:
Nina: hi all - nina here (platform infra), day 3! hitting a 403 when trying to open the Console admin panel to check feature flags for a customer repro. endpoint: GET /admin/flags. who owns role mappings for ff-operators vs ff-auditors?

Omar: welcome @Nina :wave: ff-operators are managed via the SSO group ff-operators-prod. ff-auditors are read-only. do you have staging access already?

Nina: staging yes, prod no. my goal is to view the flag state in prod to correlate with logs, not to toggle. curious if there's a service-account pattern for read-only queries so we can script checks.

Leo: we do have a service account pattern: create a service token tied to the ff-auditors group and grant it scoped read on /admin/flags. but creating service tokens for prod requires an approval ticket.

Nina: ok that works. what's the approval flow?

Claire: short answer: open a Linear ticket with rationale + owner, ping me to sponsor. Ops will create a service token OR issue a temporary JIT depending on need. include the Terraform plan if you're automating.

access-helper-bot: Access request template: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/access-requests. Use category: "service-account-read-only". Sample body: "purpose, expiry, audit owner".

Nina: pinging Claire - i filed https://linear.app/redwood/issue/PROD-5120 with steps and a one-line reason: script to snapshot prod flags for nightly health checks.

Claire: got it. sponsoring now. quick note: security prefers short-lived tokens + rotation. if this is nightly, we usually recommend a scheduled JIT that provisions a token for 1 hour at job time.

Omar: pro tip: if you only need occasional reads, use the Console UI read endpoint via the ff-auditors role instead of token embedding. then your CI can trigger a JIT before running the job.

Nina: open to JIT too. CI-triggered JIT sounds cleaner than long-lived tokens. any example?

Leo: we have a helper script in infra-tools: https://git.redwood.ai/infra-tools/jit-trigger that calls the JIT API and returns a short-lived token. you'll still need a sponsor to approve the JIT or an approver service account.

access-helper-bot: JIT-bridge created for ticket PROD-5120. Approval: Claire. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/jit/JIT-5120

Claire: approving now for a scheduled JD window. please add the automation PR with the script and a note on who owns rotation. auditors must be added to the compliance list.

Nina: approved, thanks! i'll implement the JIT-trigger and open a PR linking the Linear ticket. one more question: who do i cc for post-change audit notes?

Omar: cc @security and @ops on the ticket; include timestamps + audit id. the access-helper-bot will attach the audit id automatically when JIT completes.

Nina: perfect. thanks everyone 389. excited to get this running.
